![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/6250d388875796ad05e4d3eb8a5f625b6a633cbf0e9efb24926f72a9c6ceac7f.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by $y=1-{x}^{2}$ and $x=1-\sqrt{y},$ as shown above. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
Writing our first function in terms of $y,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}y=1-{x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{1-y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $f(y)=\sqrt{1-y}\,$ and $g(y)=1-\sqrt{y}.$

Now, we determine the limits of integration. To do that, we find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ \sqrt{1-y} & =1-\sqrt{y} \\ 1-y & =1-2\sqrt{y}+y \\ 2y-2\sqrt{y} & =0 \\ \sqrt{y}(\sqrt{y}-1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the limits of integration are from $y=0$ to $y=1.$

Let's draw our horizontal arrow through the region to determine the inner function and the outer function. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/b630edf4ad0b61defcb7aba67902f75202a8f6e9a209384fb28650c06545113f.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner function $x=g(y)=1-\sqrt{y},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $x=f(y)=\sqrt{1-y}.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({[\sqrt{1-y}]}^{2}-{[1-\sqrt{y}]}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}([1-y]-[1-2\sqrt{y}+y])\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}(2\sqrt{y}-2y)\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{1/2}-y)\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {(\frac{2{y}^{3/2}}{3}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2})|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2\pi [(\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{2})-0] \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
